board_content.text: Inverse, and 'when is it purely real?'
For real $\theta$, when is $z=\dfrac{3+2i\sin\theta}{1-2i\sin\theta}$ purely real?
Purely real means the imaginary part vanishes: $8\sin\theta=0$.

segments_english.text: Two JEE-Main flavoured examples: a multiplicative inverse, then a purely-real condition.
For z equals three minus four i, the inverse formula needs a squared plus b squared. That's nine plus sixteen, which is twenty five.
So z inverse is the conjugate three plus four i over twenty five, which we write as three twenty-fifths plus four twenty-fifths i.
Always verify: multiply three minus four i by three plus four i over twenty five. The top is nine plus sixteen, twenty five over twenty five equals one. The inverse checks out.
Now the second question. For real theta, when is z equals three plus two i sine theta, over one minus two i sine theta, purely real?

Clear the denominator by multiplying top and bottom by one plus two i sine theta. After simplifying, z becomes three minus four sine squared theta, plus eight i sine theta, all over one plus four sine squared theta.
For z to be purely real, its imaginary part must be zero. The imaginary numerator is eight sine theta, so we need eight sine theta equal to zero.
That forces sine theta equals zero, so theta is any integer multiple of pi. Clearing the denominator first is what made the imaginary part readable.

segments_hinglish.text: Do JEE-Main flavour ke examples: ek multiplicative inverse, phir ek purely-real condition.
z equals three minus four i ke liye, inverse formula ko chahiye a square plus b square. Wo hai nine plus sixteen, jo hai twenty five.
To z inverse hai conjugate three plus four i over twenty five, jise hum likhte hain three twenty-fifths plus four twenty-fifths i.
Hamesha verify karo: three minus four i ko three plus four i over twenty five se multiply karo. Top hai nine plus sixteen, twenty five over twenty five barabar one. Inverse sahi hai.
Ab doosra sawaal. Real theta ke liye, z equals three plus two i sine theta, over one minus two i sine theta, kab purely real hai?

Denominator clear karo, top aur bottom ko one plus two i sine theta se multiply karke. Simplify karne ke baad, z ban jaata hai three minus four sine square theta, plus eight i sine theta, poora over one plus four sine square theta.
z ke purely real hone ke liye, uska imaginary part zero hona chahiye. Imaginary numerator hai eight sine theta, to humein chahiye eight sine theta barabar zero.
Isse sine theta barabar zero, to theta hai pi ka koi bhi integer multiple. Pehle denominator clear karna hi imaginary part ko readable banata hai.
